footnotes.text: Reversing a sublist in place needs four handles: the node before the group, the group's first and last nodes, and the node after it. Lose one and the list falls apart.

steps.t: A dummy before the head, so the first group has a predecessor like every other group.
The group ends at 2; the next group starts at 3.
Reverse the group. prev starts at the NEXT group, so the reversed group's tail is already attached.
Reversed: 2 is now the group's first node and 1 its last.
Reconnect: the node before the group now points to 2.
1 is the new tail of the group - it becomes group_prev for the next round.
The group ends at 4; the next group starts at 5.
Reverse the group. prev starts at the NEXT group, so the reversed group's tail is already attached.
Reversed: 4 is now the group's first node and 3 its last.
Reconnect: the node before the group now points to 4.
3 is the new tail of the group - it becomes group_prev for the next round.
Fewer than 2 nodes remain - they stay as they are. Done.
Rewrote the values. (Interviewers usually forbid this: the nodes themselves must move.)
